ideas.hypothesis: Loans acquired by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac in 2005-2007 that sat near the GSE affordable-housing goal thresholds show higher default rates than similar-risk loans outside those thresholds, implying that goal pressure contributed to credit deterioration.

sources.role: measure/method: GSE loan-level data and credit event model
mechanism: policy choices in secondary mortgage markets during subprime crisis

ideas.test: GSE single-family loan-level datasets 2004-2008 merged with census tract income to identify goal-qualifying loans; regression discontinuity at tract-income thresholds on 24-month default.
ideas.disconfirming: No discontinuity in default at goal thresholds.

ideas.hypothesis: Credible resolution regimes (FSB Key Attributes, bail-in) reduce the too-big-to-fail funding advantage of large banks, measured as CDS spread gaps between G-SIBs and smaller banks.

sources.role: mechanism: FSB Key Attributes and UK resolvability reforms
setting: Swiss resilience and large financial sector

ideas.test: Panel of bank CDS spreads 2008-2019 in EU, UK, US, Switzerland; DiD around national adoption of bail-in rules, comparing G-SIBs to other banks.
ideas.disconfirming: The G-SIB funding advantage does not shrink after resolution regime adoption.

ideas.hypothesis: CLO tranches performed better than CDO tranches in 2008-2010 because of lower underlying correlation and active management, so the crisis-era portfolio diversification benefit of structured equity depended on collateral type.

sources.role: finding: CDO equity as diversifier by collateral type

ideas.test: Compare rating-transition and default rates of CLO vs ABS CDO tranches 2007-2012 from rating agency data.
ideas.disconfirming: CLOs performed no better than ABS CDOs after matching initial rating.

ideas.hypothesis: Centralized supervision (SSM) reduced the bank-sovereign doom loop: after 2014, banks' sovereign CDS sensitivity fell more in SSM-supervised than in non-SSM banks.

sources.role: mechanism: banking union addresses bank-sovereign interdependence
mechanism: lead supervisor and cross-border coordination
setting: weaknesses of national supervision in Japan

ideas.test: DiD using bank CDS and sovereign CDS 2010-2019 for SSM-significant vs less significant banks.
ideas.disconfirming: No change in sensitivity for SSM banks.

ideas.hypothesis: Countries with integrated (single) financial supervisors experienced smaller bank losses on subprime-related exposures than those with fragmented sectoral supervision.
ideas.test: Cross-country regression of 2007-2009 bank write-downs/assets on supervisory structure index for 40 countries.
ideas.disconfirming: No relation between supervisory structure and losses.

ideas.hypothesis: Emerging markets with fiscal space and lower capital-flow volatility before 2008 avoided currency crises in 2008-2009, consistent with third-generation models.

sources.role: mechanism: fiscal space during the crisis
method: structural breaks in capital flows

ideas.test: Probit for exchange market pressure crises in 50 EMs 2008-2009 on pre-crisis fiscal balance and capital-flow volatility.
ideas.disconfirming: Pre-crisis fiscal space does not predict crisis avoidance.

ideas.hypothesis: Rehypothecation limits reduce the procyclicality of shadow-bank leverage; broker-dealers in jurisdictions with caps (US Rule 15c3-3) showed smaller collateral contractions in 2008 than those under unlimited UK regimes.
ideas.test: Compare off-balance-sheet collateral received/repledged by US vs UK broker-dealer subsidiaries 2006-2010 from annual reports.

ideas.hypothesis: Banks with larger structured-product holdings pre-crisis were more likely to receive bailouts, and post-crisis Basel/FSB oversight reduced this link.

sources.role: mechanism: regulation and risk transfer via structured products

ideas.test: Logit of TARP/EU state aid receipt on 2006 structured products holdings for 200 large banks.
ideas.disconfirming: Structured product holdings do not predict bailouts.

ideas.hypothesis: Faster national adoption of Basel III capital and liquidity standards is associated with lower probability of public bailouts in subsequent stress episodes (2011-2019).

sources.role: mechanism: FSB resolution as bailout alternative

ideas.test: Country panel using BCBS RCAP adoption timing and bank state-aid events 2011-2019.

ideas.hypothesis: IMF facilities perceived as insurance (precautionary lines) produce smaller spread reductions than those perceived as positive signals; post-Asian-crisis reforms that emphasized signaling lowered contagion.

sources.role: mechanism: missing links in crisis resolution

ideas.test: Event study of EMBI spreads around IMF program announcements 1997-2010, classifying program type.
ideas.disconfirming: No difference in spread responses by program type.
